questions.question: Choose the correct form: "She ___ to school every day."
questions.explanation: A habit uses the simple present, and the third person singular takes -es: goes.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "They ___ football now."
questions.explanation: "Now" shows an action in progress, so the present continuous is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "I ___ my homework yesterday."
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" is a finished time, so the simple past is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "He ___ here since 2020."
questions.explanation: "Since 2020" takes the present perfect (has + past participle).

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "The sun ___ in the east."
questions.explanation: A universal truth takes the simple present: rises.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "We ___ a movie tomorrow."
questions.explanation: "Tomorrow" points to the future, so "will watch" is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "By the time we reached, the train ___."
questions.explanation: The train left before we reached, so the earlier action takes the past perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "She ___ for two hours when I called."
questions.explanation: An action in progress up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous: had been waiting.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "I ___ for him since morning."
questions.explanation: "Since morning" with an action that continues to now takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "While I ___ TV, the phone rang."
questions.explanation: An action in progress when another action interrupts it takes the past continuous.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "He said that he ___ the work."
questions.explanation: In reported speech after a past verb ("said"), the earlier action takes the past perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home."
questions.explanation: The if-clause uses the present tense ("rains") and the main clause uses will + base verb.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "The teacher ___ the lesson before the bell rang."
questions.explanation: Completing the lesson came before the bell, so the earlier action takes the past perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "This time next week, I ___ on a beach."
questions.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future time takes the future continuous.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "By next March, she ___ here for ten years."
questions.explanation: "By next March" points to completion before a future time, so the future perfect is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence about a past meeting.
questions.explanation: "Yesterday" is a finished time, so the simple past (saw) is used. The other options misuse the perfect or continuous forms.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence about knowing the answer.
options: She has been knowing the answer.
questions.explanation: "Know" is a stative verb and is not used in continuous forms.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "I wish I ___ the answer."
questions.explanation: After "wish" for a present situation, the past form is used: I wish I knew.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "He ___ in Pune for ten years before he moved to Hyderabad."
questions.explanation: Living in Pune was completed before the move (a past event), so the past perfect is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: "Look! It ___."
questions.explanation: "Look!" signals an action in progress now, so the present continuous is used.
